assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators and massively parallel readout turned DNA sequencing into a routine, quantitative chemical measurement and reshaped genetics, cancer biology and genome-maintenance research. The underlying nucleotide chemistry (polymerase incorporation of modified dNTPs, single-molecule/cluster readout) is concrete and general.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman are the clear originators of the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule approach; Rothberg's pyrosequencing-based 454 platform was the first commercial massively parallel system. Ju, Mayer and others contributed, so a three-person cap forces a judgment; I would anchor on the first two.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent, global use and wide reproducibility; recognition is clearly timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees sequencing as chemistry or as biology/medicine tooling.
Allocation between Solexa and 454 lineages, and the credit owed to Ju and Mayer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable cationic lipids and lipid nanoparticle formulation made systemic delivery of siRNA and mRNA possible, enabling patisiran and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. The pKa-tuned ionizable lipid is a genuine chemical design principle with enormous biomedical impact, and delivery is the step that decided whether nucleic-acid drugs work in vivo.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (including MacLachlan, Hope and Madden) built the ionizable-lipid LNP concept; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipid libraries and optimization. Credit is spread across several groups and companies, so a clean three-person split is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and independently reproduced; the 2023 Medicine prize recognized the RNA modification side, leaving delivery chemistry open and timely.
uncertainties: Fair division among the Vancouver lipid lineage and the MIT/Anderson-Langer contributions.
Patent and commercialization disputes may colour perceived credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues convert ubiquitin-ligase biology into a designable chemical modality, extending drug action to previously undruggable targets. The mechanism links chemistry to protein homeostasis and is clear and transformative for medicinal chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining glue degraders; Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray also made important contributions. The allocation is contested but a defensible trio exists.
assessment.maturity: Multiple degraders are in late-stage clinical trials with independent confirmation of mechanism, though approvals are still pending, so it is near but possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical approvals are not yet established.
Choice between PROTAC originators and the thalidomide/cereblon glue discovery as the core.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in living cells, converting translation into a programmable chemical system and giving biologists a general tool for probing and engineering proteins.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo incorporation in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and quadruplet-decoded and orthogonal ribosome systems. Yokoyama and Mehl contributed but a trio is workable.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across labs for over two decades, with a mature toolbox and continuing use; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Relative weight of the original orthogonal pair concept versus later extensions.
Therapeutic and industrial impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental and theoretical work on long-range electron tunnelling through proteins explained how redox enzymes, including radical enzymes of the type found in ribonucleotide reductase, move charge over nanometre distances, turning a biological puzzle into measurable chemical kinetics.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler drove the photochemical, ruthenium-modified-protein experiments that defined distance and pathway dependence; Marcus (already recognized) and Beratan, Onuchic and others provided theory, so the experimental pair is a coherent allocation.
assessment.maturity: Findings have been repeatedly confirmed over decades and are textbook material; the interpretation is stable, though recognition has been long delayed.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier Marcus electron-transfer prize may weaken novelty for the committee.
Contribution of theory partners such as Beratan and Onuchic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry-based proteomics lets one measure thousands of proteins and modifications in cells, a major analytical advance for all of biochemistry and medicine, including my own field's need to quantify low-abundance metabolites and proteins.
assessment.attribution: Mann (ESI/peptide proteomics, SILAC and high-resolution workflows), Aebersold (ICAT, targeted and SWATH approaches) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT) have distinct major contributions; Hunt, Heck and Gygi also qualify, so cutting to three is contested.
assessment.maturity: Ubiquitous and independently validated; but the field is broad and the 2002 ESI/MALDI prize already recognized the ionization foundation, so incremental novelty is a question.
uncertainties: Choosing three among at least six strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleotide sequence from single molecules through nanopores is an elegant physical-chemical idea turned into a deployed technology, with direct benefit to genome and nucleic-acid modification analysis.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton originated the DNA-translocation sequencing concept, Kasianowicz demonstrated single-stranded translocation, Bayley engineered protein pores with chemical adaptors, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled movement; credit is widely distributed.
assessment.maturity: Commercial instruments are in broad use and independently validated, though accuracy for some applications continues to improve and the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Credit is highly dispersed across at least five people.
Whether the scientific impact has fully matured relative to Illumina-style sequencing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite coupling chemistry made reliable automated oligonucleotide synthesis possible and underlies PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis, and nucleic-acid therapeutics; it is the chemical foundation for most work in my field.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and its solid-phase implementation; Hood's role was largely instrumentation and automation, so I propose Caruthers alone while acknowledging the supplied credit permits a pair.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with more than 40 years of universal use; recognition is very late but still fitting, and age may be a practical constraint.
uncertainties: Whether Hood or other solid-phase pioneers deserve co-credit.
Possible overlap with the 1984 Merrifield solid-phase prize concept.
